result.scientific_strategy:
## f3356be0-50ce-45d0-a495-b909a50b054c / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success, or 196/200 episodes, on the official reach-and-hold panel. The fresh baseline reached about 51% development success; reward-credit shaping reached 224/400 pooled success versus 206/400 for its unchanged control; and the transferred positive-extreme coverage recipe reached 296/400 across two disjoint panels versus 215/400 for its contemporaneous working control. A fresh replication reached 265/400 versus 288/400 for matched working controls, while recovering the positive-extreme sector on both panels. The targeted sector behavior therefore reproduced, but the aggregate improvement did not, and every measured policy remains far below the official objective. The current evidence supports preserving the reward-plus-positive-extreme recipe as a useful tested configuration while leaving its causal contribution, representation dependence, residual negative-angle failures, and hold stability unresolved.

**Lessons and limits:** Experiment 3's unchanged continuation was near-balanced with its parent and left the positive-extreme sector at zero. Experiment 2's aggressive symmetric sampler reduced overall success and degraded the strong negative-mid sector; experiment 6's gentler balanced sampler also underperformed its parent on a fresh panel and did not improve the negative-extreme sector. These results weaken coverage-only explanations without identifying whether control, representation, hold stability, or optimization is limiting. Experiment 4's reward change improved complete success and mean maximum held duration but increased interruptions and traded angular-sector performance. Experiment 5's positive-extreme focus improved the previously failing sector and measured mid sectors, while negative-extreme success remained 14/69 and its training proxies selected different checkpoints. Experiment 7 reproduced positive-extreme recovery from fresh initialization on two disjoint panels (31/31 and 34/36 for the fresh checkpoint versus 12/31 and 17/36 for working), but its pooled aggregate was lower than working (265/400 versus 288/400) and paired outcomes favored working 94-71. The fresh endpoint's stronger training proxies did not translate into higher task success and its single measured panel showed substantially more hold interruptions, so these proxies are checkpoint-selection aids rather than acceptance evidence. Complete uninterrupted hold success is authoritative; proximity, partial hold time, and training reward are incomplete signals. The task-reference panel is reused and selection-contaminated, development panels are not the official verdict, and the current 14-value observation includes target-relative geometry and inverse-kinematics angle errors but has not isolated whether an explicit continuous target-angle/radius encoding improves conditioning.
